title: Three kinds of magnetism
statement:
Which observation most directly distinguishes ferromagnetism from simple paramagnetism?

[_]{a}

choices: A sample can retain substantial magnetization after the field is removed.
An isolated atom has one unpaired electron.
A sample has a negative net charge.
explanations: Cooperative alignment can persist in a ferromagnetic material.
An atomic count does not establish bulk ferromagnetism.
This describes the usual simple diamagnetic picture.
Electric charge is not the distinction.

hints: Both can respond to an applied field.
solution: Both can respond to an applied field. Ferromagnets involve cooperative ordering. Look for retained macroscopic magnetization. Cooperative alignment can persist in a ferromagnetic material.
